wiki.content: "Break Stuff" is a song by the American band Limp Bizkit. It was released as the fourth and final single from their second studio album "Significant Other" (1999). The single was issued alongside "N 2 Gether Now" and has remained a regular part of the band’s live performances. The music video was filmed at Skatelab. It features the band members in scenes where they are both playing and not playing instruments, including sequences in which they switch instruments among themselves. The video includes cameo appearances by Snoop Dogg, Jonathan Davis of Korn, Dr. Dre, Eminem and his daughter Hailie Jade, Pauly Shore, Lily Aldridge, and Riley Hawk, the son of Tony Hawk. The video premiered in February 2000 on the USA Network program "Farmclub.com", alongside the video for "Make Me Bad" by Korn, with both bands appearing as guests to introduce their respective videos. The song is associated with several notable live performances. At Woodstock '99, its performance coincided with instances of crowd unrest. During the set, vocalist Fred Durst addressed the audience, encouraging energetic participation while also advising attendees not to harm one another. Reports from the event described crowd surges, property damage, and incidents of sexual assault. At the 2001 Big Day Out festival in Sydney, a crowd crush occurred during the band’s performance, resulting in injuries to several attendees and the death of teenager Jessica Michalik. The music video for "Break Stuff" received the MTV Video Music Award for Best Rock Video in 2000. In retrospective assessments, the song has been included in various rankings of notable nu metal tracks. In 2017, Annie Zaleski of Spin placed it seventh on a list of the best songs in the genre. In 2019, Joe Smith-Engelhardt of Alternative Press included it in a list of nu metal songs noted for their continued relevance. In 2022, publications Louder Sound and Kerrang each identified "Break Stuff" as the band’s most prominent song. In 2025, Electronic Arts featured the track in a trailer for the multiplayer mode of "Battlefield 6". Read more on Last.fm.
